summary: The paper proposes quantum amplitude-estimation algorithms to compute financial risk measures including EVaR and RVaR and evaluates them in two simulator-based case studies: a 2‑asset credit‑risk portfolio and an insurance claim dataset calibrated from 7,704 observations. Experiments on noiseless and noisy simulators (3–5 qubits for distribution loading and varying ancilla counts in QAE) show convergence toward exact values but significant noise sensitivity for CVaR and RVaR, with only theoretical quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo.
